name: nushell
one_liner: A command-line shell that treats your data as structured tables instead of plain text, making scripting less error-prone.
buyer: A data or DevOps engineer who writes a lot of brittle bash scripts and wants fewer silent failures.
business_use_cases: An ops consultancy rewrites a client's fragile bash automation in it as part of a reliability-improvement engagement, billed as a project.
A trainer sells 'modern shell scripting' workshops to ops teams tired of bash footguns.
A tooling vendor builds and sells plugin packs for common ops tasks like log parsing or cloud inventory.

money_ideas.idea: Consulting engagement rewriting brittle bash pipelines for reliability
Sell a packaged set of scripts/plugins for common ops tasks

steal_this: This is a dev tool for a shell — the only real weekend business is building and selling a niche plugin pack, like AWS or GCP inventory scripts, for ops teams who already use it.
